title: refactor(plugin-security): move the security service registration and the seed-ownership claim out of security-plugin.ts (#25223 cut 11)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMYdF2uchcinMphEKW4sYxd)_

Part of #25223
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6353073966

Cut 11 of the `security-plugin.ts` split is the first part of the `start()` row. The claim is 6373426297. Before any claim, the card thread mapped `start()` into four regions and took the plan to the seat, as cut 10's landing note asked. The seat agreed the order: this cut first, through the normal path, then cut 12 (the middleware, Tier H) claimed afresh on the merged `main`. This PR moves two seams into two new modules, unedited.

To `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-security-service.ts`:

- `registerSecurityService`, which is ONE STATEMENT of `start()`. It is the `try` that builds the `ISecurityService` literal and registers it as the `security` kernel service. That literal is what every door bypassing the engine middleware asks: the analytics raw-SQL path, the REST export route, the sharing service's management probes, `security/explain` and the metadata plane (ADR-0021 D-C, ADR-0090 D5/D6/D10/D12, ADR-0105 D3/D8, ADR-0106 D7, ADR-0111 D1/D2, ADR-0131 D3).

To `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-seed-claim.ts`:

- the body of `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle`, the seed-ownership claim that `init()` subscribes to `app:seeded` (ADR-0138 D1);
- the two readers it asks the published `seed-settlement` contract through, `readSeedSettlementSnapshot` and `readSeededRecordIds`.

The change is move-only, and the card stays open for cut 12. The branch is `claude/project-thread-3fzya4`, the harness-pinned branch for this session. It was restarted from `origin/main` at `82f5a111b4`, which contains cut 10's merge. The branch name names no issue, so the claim comment is the identity record.

## How one statement of `start()` moves

This is the first cut to move a statement out of a method rather than a whole method body. The seat agreed the plan's form for it before the claim.

- The statement is `:2266`-`:2560` at base (295 lines). It closes over three of `start()`'s locals and nothing else: `ctx`, `ql` and `metadata`. It uses no `arguments`, `super`, `new.target` or bare `this`. It has no `return`, `await`, `break` or `continue` at its top level that would act on `start()`. All of that was measured on the AST.
- So the function takes the three locals as parameters, typed as the statement saw them there: `PluginContext`, `IObjectQLEngine` and `IMetadataService`. Both handles are already known to be present at that point. Its body is the statement, re-indented one level and otherwise unedited. It returns `void`, as the statement produced no value.
- `start()` keeps the statement's position and the comment above it (`:2259`-`:2265`). In its place is one BLOCK: the getter reads, one host literal annotated with the `Pick` of `SecurityServiceHost`, and `registerSecurityService.call(host, ctx, ql, metadata);`. Because it is a block, its `const`s stay inside it and cannot collide with anything later in `start()`.
- The statement ran synchronously and still does. The call is in the same place in `start()`'s order: after the invitation placement service is registered and before the middleware is registered.

## What moved

The base line numbers are at `82f5a111b4`. The last column lists the members the moved code reads, which is exactly what its host carries.

| code | base lines | module | host members |
|---|---|---|---|
| the `security` service registration (one statement of `start()`) | `:2266`-`:2560` | security-service | methods: `canExport`, `canReadObject`, `checkAuthoredRowWrite`, `checkControlledByParentWrite`, `declareEveryone`, `describePositionGrants`, `explainAccessForCaller`, `getEffectiveObjectPermissions`, `getMetadataReadableFields`, `getObjectSecurityMeta`, `getQueryableFields`, `getReadFilter`, `getReadableFields`, `getWritableFields`, `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`; by value: `acceptedDefaultPermissionSets`, `ownershipFloorAlternates`; getters: `delegatedAdminGate`, `logger`, `permissionEvaluator`, `ql`, `tenancyPosture` |
| `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` (private, async) | `:1873`-`:1905` | seed-claim | by value: `bootstrapPermissionSets`; getter: `claimTargetAdminUserId` |
| `readSeedSettlementSnapshot` (module function, with its docblock) | `:1254`-`:1273` | seed-claim | none |
| `readSeededRecordIds` (module function, with its docblock) | `:1275`-`:1293` | seed-claim | none |

- `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` keeps its name, signature, docblock and position, less `async`. It returns the moved function's promise, as cuts 1 and 3 to 10 did for their async methods. `init()`'s `app:seeded` subscription still calls it on the plugin.
- The two readers move with their docblocks, unedited, and gain `export` and nothing else. `security-plugin.ts` imports both back, because R4's promotion-time pass on `kernel:ready` reads both (`:4550`, `:4590`).
  - Why they move rather than gain `export` where they stood: each signature names a contract type. Cut 6 measured that an export from `security-plugin.ts` whose signature names another module's type reorders the `.d.ts`. So they moved, and the `.d.ts` was measured anyway (below).
- Import names that only the moved code reads leave `security-plugin.ts`, 16 in all. The modules import them from the same specifiers.
  - From the registration:
    - `resolveDelegatorContext`, `delegatedOrganizationRefusal` and `d10NarrowingStatement` (`./explain-engine.js`);
    - `listAudienceBindingSuggestions`, `confirmAudienceBindingSuggestion`, `dismissAudienceBindingSuggestion` and the types `SuggestionDeps` and `SuggestionListFilter` (`./suggested-audience-bindings.js`);
    - the type `OwnershipFloorAlternate` (`./platform-ownership-policies.js`);
    - the type `ObjectAccessScope` (`@objectstack/spec/security`);
    - the types `ISecurityService` and `DelegationNarrowing` (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`).
  - From the seed claim:
    - `SEED_SETTLEMENT_SERVICE` and the type `ISeedSettlementService` (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`);
    - `findExistingPlatformAdmin` (`./bootstrap-platform-admin.js`);
    - the whole `./claim-seed-ownership.js` import (`claimSeedOwnership`).
  - Disclosed: one staying docblock, `computeDelegatedReadFilter`'s, names `resolveDelegatorContext` in a `{@link}`. The name is no longer imported, so that link is now plain text, like the bare-member `{@link computeRlsFilter}` beside it. No docblock is edited. Every other staying mention of a dropped name is in backticks or prose.
- Each value import is read only inside a function body, at call time, never while a module evaluates. `index.ts` exports only what it did, so the published surface does not move (measured below).

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1 to 10 applied it)

- `SecurityServiceHost` and `SeedClaimHost` are new. Each types every member as the class member itself (`SecurityPlugin['m']`). Each moved function types its `this` as the `Pick` of its host over exactly the members its code reads, and the stub annotates its literal with the same `Pick`. There is no cast, and no member becomes public or protected.
- Methods go in as late-bound closures that call `this.m(...a)` on the plugin at call time. Every member of the registered service that binds a plugin method was already an arrow calling `this.m(…)`. `this.m` is now the host's closure, which calls the plugin's method on the plugin. So every call reaches the same method on the same receiver, and a spy or test double set on the plugin is still the one the service reaches.
- Fields follow the rule cut 1 set, judged on each field's own declaration:
  - `acceptedDefaultPermissionSets`, `ownershipFloorAlternates` and `bootstrapPermissionSets` are declared `readonly`, so they go by value: the same object references.
  - `delegatedAdminGate`, `logger`, `permissionEvaluator`, `ql`, `tenancyPosture` and `claimTargetAdminUserId` are not. So they go as getters, and each read happens when the code makes it. For example, the posture the suggestion deps hand out is still read per call, and the claim still reads the admin R4 names when it runs.
  - None of them is function-valued: each is an object whose own methods the code calls, or a value it reads. No receiver changes.
  - The hosts declare every field `readonly`, so moved code cannot assign a member through them. The typecheck passes, so none does. Neither moved region writes a member.
- Nothing re-exports either module, so the package entry does not move.

## Three readers read the moved lines by path, and all three are re-pointed in this PR

These are the three the seat named. Each was run with its edit reverted, and each fails without it.

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`, row 7. The registration holds 3 of `start()`'s 4 `isSystem` reads: `hasWriteBypass`'s, `resolveWriteScope`'s and `describeDelegationNarrowing`'s system short-circuits. `check-system-context-census` keys each read by file and enclosing symbol, so row 7's anchor changes from `security-plugin.ts#start` to `security-plugin-security-service.ts#registerSecurityService`.
  - The symbol changes because the reads now sit in the function. The row's text and every other anchor stay. Rows 1, 2 and 30 keep `#start`, which still holds the middleware's read.
  - With the page untouched, the census reports 1 problem: `[file-without-a-row]` for the new module. With the re-point it exits 0.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts`, the #25107 enumeration pin. The registration holds the only delegator resolution in `security-plugin.ts`, and the organization ask beside it. So in the expected list, `security-plugin-security-service.ts` replaces `security-plugin.ts`, and the count stays at seven files.
  - The rule it pins is unchanged: asks equal resolutions in every file. It holds: the new module has 1 and 1, and `security-plugin.ts` has 0 and 0.
  - Unedited, it fails on the list.
- `packages/core/src/security/row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts`. Every file that calls `canReadObject` must be classified, and the service literal's binding `this.canReadObject(…)` now sits in the new module.
  - The new module gains a `not-a-door` entry: "the provider's service registration: it binds the admission into the `security` service the plugin registers; it serves no rows".
  - `security-plugin.ts` stays a caller, through the stub's closure and `describePositionGrants`' own ask. Its reason no longer says it binds the admission into the service. It now says "the provider: it implements the admission, hands it to its service registration, and asks it itself only to decide whether `describePositionGrants` may count a position's holders; it serves no rows".
  - Unedited, it fails with the new module unclassified.

## One new anchor entry

`scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin-seed-claim.ts.json` (`adrs: ["ADR-0138"]`).

- Its invariant is the ADR-0138 D1 paragraph of the `security-plugin.ts` entry, verbatim. That paragraph names `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` and `readSeededRecordIds`, whose bodies now sit in the module. Cut 9 carried ADR-0106 D7 into `security-plugin-field-readers.ts` the same way.
- The `security-plugin.ts` entry is unchanged and stays true: the method, the promotion-time pass and the import of `readSeededRecordIds` stay in that file.
- The security-service module gets no entry, because no paragraph describes the registration:
  - ADR-0055 §1 is the relation reader;
  - ADR-0106 D7 is the readable-field asymmetry, in the field-readers module since cut 9;
  - ADR-0123 D2 is step 3.7's refusal, in the middleware.

`docs/adr/**` is not touched, and no other governed path is, so this is a normal landing.

## The published `.d.ts` does not change

Measured under the series bar (ruling 6348891160 item 1), on base `82f5a111b4` and on head `5a4747b9c7`. Each was a full `turbo run build` in its own worktree (both exit 0).

- Raw sha256 of `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` is the same for all four files, base and head: `5e7e8df69375e6606767eee938111aaaf0b9bac4dd9c728689c343be9e5f7702` (14,696 lines). The raw diff is 0 lines, so no union order moved either.
- Normalised sha256 is the same for all four: `1e2e8299c2b3aa8502ae3684a5a8a4f7148b2211876a0a581f20d27677531ed9`.
- `security-plugin.ts` gains no export. The two readers gained `export` in the new module, which nothing re-exports, so the cut 6 trap does not arise.
- The normaliser, run from `packages/plugins/plugin-security`, sorts the members of each string-literal union and changes nothing else:

```sh
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8");process.stdout.write(s.replace(/"[^"\n]*"(?:\s*\|\s*"[^"\n]*")+/g,r=>r.split(/\s*\|\s*/).sort().join(" | ")))' dist/index.d.ts | sha256sum
```

- Positive control, a real package build rather than an edit of the emitted file. With `private` removed from `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` in the head source, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security build` emits line 431 as the full public signature instead of `private claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle;`. That gives raw `12beec21603e70025c7a1b70d2c49fd0dd110d66a61b57e82098a6eb903fe08c` and normalised `0509461ad52776d160e6875c3a99cee28dda954089413b05db158aabda6d52ff`, both different from the real hashes. So the comparison does see a visibility change. With the source restored, a rebuild gives `5e7e8df6…` again for both files.
- `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` is private, so the `.d.ts` carries only its name and docblock (line 431). `registerSecurityService` and the two readers are in no published file.
- Export tables: the ESM and CJS bundles each export the same 66 names at base and at head. The lists were loaded at runtime, with `require` and `import()` of the built bundles, not parsed. The sorted name list hashes to `83576430f83cf60cecbcc5c0e80214f16c626a8e66f700294fc6a44361423116` for all four, as at cuts 6 to 10.
- The bundle JS bytes differ, because code moved within them: `index.js` goes from `a0d05e78` to `b734b9f0`, and `index.mjs` from `1080b070` to `51498bc7`. Every value the new modules import comes from a file inside this package or from a specifier `security-plugin.ts` already imports. So the set of external specifiers each bundle loads is the same at base and head: 17 distinct `require(…)` specifiers in `index.js` and 24 distinct `from` specifiers in `index.mjs`, counted the same way at both ends.
- Bundle order, disclosed. The seed-claim module imports `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` and `claim-seed-ownership.ts`. So those two, and `platform-admin-standing-audit.ts`, are now emitted after the two new modules and ahead of `ownership-floor-alternates.ts` and `security-plugin.ts`'s first chunk, instead of after `predicate-guard.ts`. None of the three imports `security-plugin.ts`. Their top level only declares (one constant is computed from an imported constant, `CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS`).

No changeset: `skip-changeset`, per ruling 6348891160 item 4.

## Proof of move-only

- **The statement, by AST token.** `registerSecurityService`'s body is one statement, with the same TypeScript token sequence as the base `try` statement: 1,296 tokens. Each of its 295 lines is the base line with two leading spaces removed. Multi-line JSDoc text tokens inside it are re-indented one level, like every other line, so the comparison dedents those tokens one level, and only those.
- **`start()` outside the statement.** The head text of `start()` equals the base text exactly, outside the one statement, which is now a 33-line stub block ending in the `.call`. Its signature, docblock and every other statement are byte-identical. That covers R1, the comment above the statement, the middleware and R4.
- **The method, by AST token.** `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle`'s function body has the same token sequence as the base method body (136 tokens), and each of its 28 lines is the base line less two spaces. The parameters, the return type and `async` match. The class keeps the method's docblock and signature, less `async`.
- **The two readers.** Each one's text in the module, docblock included, is the base text with `export` added, and nothing else. Neither is left in `security-plugin.ts`.
- **Class side.** Every other class member is byte-identical to base: 124 named members plus the constructor. The class has 127 members at base and at head.
- **Top level of `security-plugin.ts`.** Of the 110 top-level statements at base other than the class, 101 are byte-identical at head. The other nine are:
  - six imports that each lose the names listed above;
  - the `./claim-seed-ownership.js` import, which is gone;
  - the two readers, which are gone from the file.

  The two new statements are the imports of the new modules, with their comments. The check asserts the exact list of 16 dropped names and 6 added names, and that no dropped name is still referenced in the file.
- **Negative controls.** Seven fail the check:
  - in the registration, `ctx.logger.info(` changed to `ctx.logger.debug(`;
  - in the registration, one line indented by one more space, with the tokens unchanged;
  - in `start()`, one edit in R1 (`:1914`), ahead of the stub;
  - in `start()`, one edit in the middleware, after the stub;
  - in `readSeedSettlementSnapshot`, `return undefined` changed to `return null`;
  - in `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle`, `ctx.logger.warn(` changed to `ctx.logger.error(`;
  - in a top-level docblock of `security-plugin.ts`, one trailing space added.
- **git's own view.** This is `git diff --color-moved=plain --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change 82f5a111b4 HEAD` over the three source files.
  - Of the 378 deleted lines, git sees 370 as moved. The other 8 are four type-import lines and the `./bootstrap-platform-admin.js` import line, which the modules group differently; the two reader signatures that gain `export`; and the method signature that loses `async`.
  - Of the 613 added lines, 391 show as moved: 311 in the security-service module, 79 in the seed-claim module, and 1 in `security-plugin.ts` (a stub's `};`). The rest are the modules' headers, imports, host interfaces and function signatures, the two stubs, and the two new imports with their comments.
- **Size.** 1,010 changed lines (+629 / -381) over 7 files, under the 3,000-line manual-merge line.
  - `security-plugin.ts` goes from 8,442 to 8,120 lines.
  - `security-plugin-security-service.ts` has 418 lines, and `security-plugin-seed-claim.ts` 139.
  - The other four files are the page (+1 / -1), the two pins (+1 / -1 and +7 / -1) and the anchor entry (+7).

## ADR anchors (ruling 6353073966 item 2)

- `node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs` exits 0 and gives the same output at base `82f5a111b4` and at head.
- `pnpm check:adr-anchors` exits 0 at base and at head. Anchored files go from 82 to 83, the new entry.
- **The decision-letter count on the anchored surface goes from 1970 to 1958.** That gate counts `ADR-NNNN Dk` citations in each anchored file and in each entry's own invariant text. The −12 is:
  - −13: the registration's letters leave the anchored surface with it (ADR-0090 D5 three times, D6, D10 and D12; ADR-0105 D3 and D8; ADR-0106 D7 twice; ADR-0111 D1 and D2; ADR-0131 D3);
  - 0: `readSeededRecordIds`' docblock carries ADR-0138 D1, and it stays on the anchored surface, now in an anchored module;
  - +1: the new entry's invariant text.

  The method body, the module headers, the stubs and the new import comments cite none. Measured per file: `security-plugin.ts` holds 250 such citations at base and 236 at head. The security-service module holds the 13, and the seed-claim module the 1.
- Every moved citation is still in the tree, in the module its code moved to. Citations that resolve tree-wide go from 52262 across 6671 files at base to 52264 across 6674 at head. The two added citations are the new entry's `adrs` list and its invariant. The three added files are the two modules and the entry.
- `docs/adr/**` is not touched, and no anchor token is planted.
- The anchor map covers every ADR symbol anchor that names `security-plugin.ts`: 18 symbols.
  - It was measured with `extractAnchors` and `symbolSegmentResolution` from `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`. That is measurement, not a new gate.
  - It was read on `82f5a111b4` BEFORE the claim, with the whole cut applied as a local trial, and no anchor changed class.
  - No ADR anchors the moved method, the two readers or the new function. Two anchored members are named inside the service literal: `#getReadFilter` and `#SecurityPlugin.getMetadataReadableFields`. Their names now also appear in the stub's host literal and its `Pick`. Both still resolve as `declaration`, on the methods.

## Readers

The three readers above are the only ones that read the moved lines by path. No other gate, baseline, docs anchor or test does. Each kind was read:

- **The system-context census.**
  - `node scripts/isystem-census.mjs --json` gives the same 149 sites at base and at head, with 0 differences. The comparison ignores line numbers, maps the two modules back to `security-plugin.ts`, and maps the symbol `registerSecurityService` back to `start`.
  - Three head sites are in the security-service module: the three short-circuits, which the re-pointed row 7 names.
  - The role counts are the same (`read` 154, `declaration` 39, `key` 440, `other` 9), and so are the 5 non-elevation reads. Files holding a site go from 76 to 77, and scanned files from 402 to 403.
  - `check-system-context-census` and its `--self-test` exit 0 at base and at head. The totals: 149 sites at both; symbols 128 to 129; cited 141 to 142 against as many required; files 76 to 77. With the page untouched, it reports 1 problem (above).
- **The tenant-audit census.** No moved code holds an engine write. The seed claim writes through `claimSeedOwnership`, which stays in its own file, and the registration only reads.
  - `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --json` gives the same 238 write call sites at base and at head, compared the same way: 0 differences, none in the modules, and the same 176 non-engine calls. Only `scannedSources` moves, from 739 to 741: the two modules.
  - `check-tenant-audit-census` exits 0 at base and at head, and `tenant-audit-census.mdx` is not touched.
- **The two pins** are described above. `operation-private-keys.pin.test.ts` (`@objectstack/core`) names no moved code, and it passes at head.
- **Symbol anchors outside the ADRs.** Across the ADR, spec liveness, platform checklist, system-context page and spec `conversions/registry.ts` corpora, `security-plugin.ts#X` is cited 48 times over 26 symbols at base and 47 at head. With `symbolSegmentResolution`, each resolves at head with its base class: 0 changed. The one ref that leaves is row 7's.
  - `check-platform-checklist` (the script and `pnpm check:platform-checklist`), `check-scripts-symbol-anchors` and its `--self-test`, and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness` were run at base and at head (Gates).
- **Readers by name, not by path.** These were read, and none needs a change:
  - the behaviour tests of the `security` service and the seed claim in this package. Each drives the plugin or the registered service, and none calls the moved code directly. No test replaces `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` on the plugin instance;
  - the page's row text and the docblocks that stay in the class, which name these members and stay true by name.
- **Line citations.** No `security-plugin.ts:N` citation in the repo points into the moved ranges (base `:1254` to `:1293`, `:1873` to `:1905` and `:2266` to `:2560`).

## Gates

All gates ran against base `82f5a111b4` and on head `5a4747b9c7`, each in its own worktree after a full `turbo run build` there (both exit 0). The CI run on this head is green: 36 checks passed and 11 were skipped by their path filters.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test` (`vitest run`): Test Files 218 passed (218); Tests 4573 passed, 45 skipped (4618). Base `82f5a111b4` gives the same counts.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: exit 0 at head and at base. It runs `tsc --noEmit`, the scripts tsconfig, and `check:test-typecheck`.
- eslint over the five touched source and test files: exit 0.
